parallel.requirements: The parent and children recognized the Python source, required pure ESM .mjs outputs, exact CLI argument behavior, local-only imports, and a final /output/test6.mjs deliverable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation authority while spawning /root/probe_cli and /root/find_rules, but the children also implemented and wrote output files rather than staying isolated to research.
parallel.implementation: The run produced multiple module graphs for CLI parsing and bidirectional lookup. The parent first wrote one lib/core and lib/cli graph, a child wrote a different cli/core graph, another child wrote root-level modules, and the parent later hardened the chosen root-level graph.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was reactive: after observing test6.mjs changing, the parent inspected competing files, identified a background agent as the source of churn, preserved the newer entry/module graph, and left both root-level and alternate nested modules in the artifact.
parallel.verification: The parent and children ran many executable and Node spot checks for normal output, help text, missing args, invalid integers, abbreviations, and unusual negative or underscore tokens; the parent ended with an all-parity-checks-passed local script.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation still failed 6 of 163 samples. The trajectory does not expose a parent-visible unresolved evaluator case, and the same 157/163 result appears in serial.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual process.argv, no external dependency, output formatting, and /output/test6.mjs delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, verification, cleanup, and final response, with no subagent activity or handoff boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote one five-file ESM implementation: program name handling, integer parsing, CLI parser, bidirectional lookup, and the test6.mjs entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was integrated in one patch and later lightly trimmed; the official artifact contains only the one intended entry and root-level library files.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran Node checks against normal, help, missing argument, invalid value, unknown argument, empty/equal forms, repeated flags, and signed integer cases, then retested the sample after cleanup.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation also failed 6 of 163 samples, so hidden edge behavior remained imperfect despite the single-agent workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the exact ESM, manual argv parsing, zero external dependency, and /output/test6.mjs requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt and task requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both aimed at the same CLI and bidirectional membership behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned /root/probe_cli and /root/find_rules while also implementing in the root workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child agents and the single agent owned the whole pipeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split work across several live actors without isolating implementation ownership; serial kept one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were opaque in the ledger, but child actions show they treated /output as writable implementation space rather than only returning research.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context transfer and planned one local parser/library interface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important contrast is not a proven missing brief; it is that the parallel actors independently acted on the same delivery surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel generated an initial parent graph, then child-generated cli/core files, then a separate root-level graph that the parent later hardened.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial generated one root-level module graph and made only a small cleanup edit afterward.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation path involved competing code histories; serial's was linear.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent observed child activity, received the find_rules result, and interrupted remaining child work after the conflict was visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it verified and finalized its own work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required monitoring and consolidation of external child work, while serial had no join or child-return step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several live agents wrote the shared /output workspace and competing required entry files, and the parent explicitly reported the entry was flipping between implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the output tree once and its artifact contains the expected single root-level library set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main adverse contrast: parallel had a concrete deliverable overwrite and serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ultimately ran a parity script and reported all checked cases passed after consolidation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran representative Node checks and retested the sample after cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used sampled/local checks rather than the hidden official suite; parallel verification had to happen after resolving shared-state churn.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed more wall-clock and tool budget with three spawned child calls, 520 agent seconds, and 304 tool calls, but still completed without timing out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 174 agent seconds with 56 tool calls and no child activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used substantially more coordination budget, mostly around probing and reconciling multiple implementations, but there is no evidence of budget exhaustion causing unfinished required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show no discordant outcome: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false with 157 passed of 163 total samples. The parallel-specific adverse event was shared deliverable overwrite and reconciliation, but the serial control reached the same official score, so the evidence supports a process penalty rather than an official outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced competing /output implementations and the parent had to stabilize the final entry/module graph after detecting churn.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and wrote one implementation path, but still failed the same hidden official cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts locally verified sampled argparse and membership behavior but left six hidden evaluator samples failing; the exact hidden shortfall is not directly visible from the trajectory.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process episode only

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by the parent and also by child agents; the problem was overlapping ownership, not absence of an implementer.
The parent explicitly inspected competing module graphs and consolidated the final implementation, so integration ownership was present.
The parent delivered /output/test6.mjs and final artifact validation found the expected entry file, so assembly was not unowned.
The parent owned the end-to-end flow through probing, consolidation, verification, and final response despite shared-state interference.
Implementation was not blocked behind a single mandatory preflight; parent and children probed and implemented in overlapping windows.
The run did not complete all investigation before starting implementation; the parent and children wrote code while other probing continued.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the parent completed a deliverable and verified it after resolving the write conflict.
The run used more agents, tokens, and time than serial, but it did not exhaust the run budget or leave required work unfinished because of fan-out.
No single child received a demonstrably overbroad assignment that remained unfinished; the adverse chain is better classified as a write collision.
The child task bodies are encrypted in the raw record, and the child behavior shows awareness of the same CLI and /output requirements rather than unusable work from a missing requirement.
The children did not merely return incompatible APIs; they concretely wrote and replaced the same required entry point, so the write-event label takes precedence.
No known finding is shown disappearing during transfer; the parent consumed child output and file state when resolving the conflict.
Child outputs and handoffs were not too large to consume; the parent inspected and acted on the available implementation state.
The parent did not rely on a stale handoff; it noticed the workspace had changed and reread the current files before finalizing.
The conflict manifested as concrete file replacement in /output, not as unresolved conflicting reports handed back to the parent.
The parent ran integrated local parity checks after consolidation, and no parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap appears before closure; hidden evaluator failures alone do not qualify.
There is no replacement or retry that repeats prior work without inherited findings; multiple agents worked concurrently rather than through retry turnover.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: A child was interrupted after producing competing files, but the needed remaining work was taken over through parent consolidation; the direct adverse event is the overwrite.
A final deliverable was placed and verified before closure; no complete promotable candidate was left unfinalized by timing.
The parent reran verification after settling the final implementation, so there is no unverified post-check merge.
The parent inspected and used the child-produced implementation state instead of leaving a retrievable implementation unjoined.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent; available child information reached or was inspected by the parent.
No required child failure was abandoned; after the conflict appeared, the parent took over by reading, patching, and verifying the final state.
The parent did not ignore an available completed child result; it received the find_rules result and used the workspace state to guide consolidation.
There were wait attempts, but the parent actively inspected files and agent status during the period; no blind wait displaced a needed action.
Competing designs existed across files, but same deliverable replacement is directly evidenced and has higher precedence.
Two live agents wrote the same file, but that file was the required executable entry point and was overwritten, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
Library modules were also affected, but the same episode includes replacement of the entry deliverable, which takes precedence over non-entry source overwrite.

Parallel live agents independently replaced /output/test6.mjs, the required executable entry point, while the parent and children were still testing and editing; the parent then had to reconcile the churn.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required entry file changed during active testing, forcing parent reconciliation and leaving extra alternate module files in the final artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but the overwritten file was the submitted executable entry point, so the deliverable-specific label wins.

candidates.reason: The evidence shows competing patches to individual implementation paths rather than a broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced the whole final tree.
The workspace was shared and unisolated, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven for the same episode.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact was consumed as a stable reference environment; the issue was direct output overwrite.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent spawned children into the same workspace, and live child agents wrote competing versions of /output/test6.mjs, the required executable entry point. The parent then observed the file changing underneath it, identified background-agent churn, and had to consolidate before final verification. Serial wrote one entry/module graph with no competing deliverable writer.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The required entry file changed during active testing, forcing parent reconciliation and leaving extra alternate module files in the final artifact.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but the overwritten file was the submitted executable entry point, so the deliverable-specific label wins.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes are suppressed because they describe the same competing-write chain at lower precedence.

Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Missing Implementation Join are suppressed or rejected because the parent inspected and consolidated rather than abandoning a necessary child result.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no additional independent adverse parallel episode cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained label uses one episode and one consequence; nearby write and lifecycle symptoms were not split into additional labels.
